https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/bl.title: Blind and deaf fox cubs make miraculous recovery after builders find them alone in den
https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/bl.subtitle: The cubs were days old with their eyes still closed when contractors removing a wall at a building site found them and called the Harper Asprey Wildlife Rescue centre in Windlesham, Surrey, in spring 2019
https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/bl.text:
A litter of fox cubs were dubbed the Magnificent Seven after they were found alone in their den by builders and hand reared at a rescue centre before being released into the wild.
The cubs were days old, with their eyes still closed, when contractors removing a wall at a building site found them and called the Harper Asprey Wildlife Rescue centre in Windlesham, Surrey, in spring 2019.
Anne Brummer, who heads up the centre, said: “We were called out after the two builders initially found one thinking it was a kitten, then realised it was a fox cub.
“But as they removed the cubs, others kept falling out of this hole, and the builders kept catching them and ended up with seven.
“It was unusual to see that number together.”
The four male and three female cubs, named Do, Re, Mi, Fa, So, La and Ti, needed 24-hour care.
Anne said: “They were blind and deaf as they were so young they hadn’t developed these senses yet. They all needed regular feeding.
“But the foxes all went from strength to strength and we could see their personalities developing.”
They were successfully released into the wild in July 2019, are the stars of a two-part documentary, starting tonight on Channel 5.
Narrated by naturalist Steve Backshall, Fantastic Foxes: Their Secret World takes a look at one of the UK’s most divisive creatures.
Red foxes are the world’s most successful carnivore and the most widespread animal, living in every continent bar Antarctica. Steve said: “They are such a survivalist, they are resourceful, they are supremely adaptable to every single situation.
“There are few animals that polarise opinion like the fox does. So much about them is remarkable that we don’t understand, as so much of their world happens out of sight.”
For the series, cameras were put into a den to see how vixens give birth and behave with their cubs.
And the Magnificent Seven gave a unique opportunity for Keele University scientist Professor Dawn Scott to study how foxes gain their personalities, how much is down to nature or nurture.
The seven all thrived in the wild, five of them still regularly spotted.
Anne said: “We see them on our trap cameras. Mi had cubs this year. We didn’t see La for ages, but she appeared back in the winter."

https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-n.title: Katie Price 'planning holiday to reset' before returning to work after alleged attack
https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-n.subtitle: Former glamour model Katie Price is reportedly planning to jet off on another holiday abroad so she can have some 'time and space' before resuming her work commitments
https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-n.text:
Katie Price is reportedly planning to jet off on another holiday so she can enjoy some "time and space" before returning to work after she was allegedly assaulted.
The former glamour model, 43, who recently returned from a trip to St Lucia, pulled out of plans to return to the spotlight on Friday with an appearance at the British LGBT Awards.
She is now taking some time to rest and is said to be planning another holiday to help her recharge.
A source told The Sun : "Her management team have told her there’s no rush to return to work but Katie would like to get back to normal as quickly as she can and if she can get back to work for a bit next week she will.
"She’s also thinking about jetting off for a few days away next month to get some more time and space."
It comes days after Katie was left "devastated and dazed" following an alleged assault at a house in Essex in the early hours of Monday morning.
She was taken to hospital to treat facial injuries and is also said to have damaged her feet again after previously breaking bones on both sides during a holiday in Turkey last year.
She told The Sun : "I’ve got a big bruise, my face is all puffy, and I went to hospital.
"I'm still all dazed. I’m devastated. I’ve told police that I was assaulted, and am in shock that this happened...
"I ran to [son] Harvey's house and have now done damage to my feet, which I previously injured."
A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of assault, theft and coercive and controlling behaviour.
He's been released on bail until September 20.
A statement from Essex Police said: "A man arrested on suspicion of assault, theft and coercive and controlling behaviour has been released on bail until September 20."
After the alleged attack, Katie is said to be suffering from sleepless nights and flashbacks.
A source told MailOnline : "Katie is in a terrible state at the moment.
"She has woken up more than once after having nightmares about what happened.
"She keeps getting flashbacks and keeps replaying what went on over and over again. It is tormenting her which is really sad to see. Her friends are doing their best to rally round."
As well as stepping away from work in recent days, Katie has also quit social media following a barrage of abuse from trolls.
Confirming Katie was taking time away, her representative told the Mirror: "Katie will make a return to her social in due course."

https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news.title: Whole street slides down hill and homes split in half as furious families left homeless
https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news.subtitle: A street in Gold Coast City in Australia has seen whole swimming pools move as angry residents blame the council and the developer for not fixing the issues sooner
https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news.text:
Heavy rain in Australia saw an entire street of homes slide down a hill into the path of other houses, with one property even splitting in half.
Residents of a new housing development on the Gold Coast are furious after at least seven homes on two streets have been affected by the rain-caused damage.
A number of families have had to leave their homes following the downpour, reports a local news site.
Those affected have called the developers behind the new housing "big fat liars" and say they have been treated "disgracefully" during the disaster.
A house in Riverstone Crossing in a Maudsland suburb reportedly split in half, with two massive cracks running through the building.
And it's not just the houses themselves that have been affected by the heavy rainfall.
Swimming pools have sunk and moved, walls have collapsed and outside decking has been destroyed.
Local resident Jason Lyall, who lives with his wife, Amber, and their three children on the road told news.com that the damage has been "catastrophic".
He told news.com.au : “Every night it rained I was skittish. I couldn’t sleep because I kept thinking is this going to be another Thredbo landslide where you go to sleep and never wake up?”
It's almost certain that the Lyall family's home will have to be demolished - they are currently renting a two-bedroom home while they wait for news.
Mr Lyall said the developer and the council are to blame, claiming that the former didn't meet the development conditions and the latter signed the work off as 'complete' despite this.
The developer has said it carried out all the work necessary to make the homes safe and was offering to buy them at 'above market' value.
A spokesperson told news.com.au “Since the significant rainfall and landslip event, our priority has been the safety and support of residents."
But Mr Lyall said the firm failed to build an adequate sub-surface drain system, which would have diverted water away from homes and so stopped the damage.
The family began building their dream home, costing $1 million AUS (£530k), on the empty space on Greenvale Crescent in 2018.
It has four bedrooms, three living spaces, a huge garage and an infinity pool and was all the family wanted for the next 20-25 years.
They moved in back in 2019, but less than two years later have had to move back out again.
Mr Lyall said the proper processes were completed and he had no reason to suspect the Stockland estate wasn't safe for him to build on.
The Gold Coast was hit with significant rainfall in March 2021, and it's from then that the street has started to face issues.
One neighbour noticed his retaining walls had started moving towards his home. Mr Lyall noted that his pool began to drop, and then things started to worse and worse as the weeks and months went on.
He described how the pool has dropped and moved by around a metre while the initially strong decking has crumbled.
The home next to the Lyall house has nearly split in two.
With at least seven homes being affected and moving as a result of this, there has been significant movement towards other houses.
“If there’s another big rain event you would probably have at least two houses, a couple of pools sliding down the hill towards other houses below,” Mr Lyall told the news site.
A spokesperson for Gold Coast City Council said “compliance investigations into the conditions of the development’s approval are ongoing”.
